reason: The hypothesis merges multiple distinct findings, but the cited evidence does not support the combined approach. E7/E8 show properties of amorphous AlTiVNb films, but no evidence links this to SRO quantification (E1/E2), Ti doping (E3/E4), or Si/Ta additions (E5/E6) in the same alloy system. The premises are individually supported for different materials, but the key premise that merging these specific interventions in a single HEA will yield improved combinations of properties is unsupported by any cited evidence.
premises: Amorphous AlTiVNb HEA films exhibit high strength and ductility due to disordered state, nanostructure, and lattice distortion
SRO in HEAs can be quantified by atom probe tomography and engineered by heat treatments
Ti addition increases hardness and erosion resistance in AlCoCrFeNi-based HEAs
Si addition improves mechanical properties and fracture behavior in TiMoZrTa-based HEAs
Ta addition contributes to tensile strength and Young's modulus decrease in Ti-based HEAs
